q: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one _____ bond.
e: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one C-C or C-H bond.

q: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms are bonded to each other by _____ bonds.
e: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms are bonded to each other by covalent bonds.

q: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called _____ hydrocarbons.
e: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons.

q: Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes, alkynes and _____ compounds.
e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes, alkynes and aromatic compounds.

q: The _____ formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule.
e: The molecular formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule.

q: A full structural formula shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the _____ geometry of the molecule.
e: A full structural formula shows every bond and atom but does not portray accurately the three-dimensional geometry of the molecule.

q: A _____ structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule.
e: A condensed structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule.

q: A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms that determine the _____ properties of a compound.
e: A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms that determine the chemical properties of a compound.

q: An alcohol is an organic compound with a _____ functional group attached to a carbon atom.
e: An alcohol is an organic compound with a hydroxyl (-OH) functional group attached to a carbon atom.

q: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula _____, where R is an alkyl group.
e: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl group.

q: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same functional group and similar structure and whose structures differ only by the number of _____ units in the main carbon chain.
e: A homologous series differs only by the number of $CH_2$ units in the main carbon chain.

q: In a homologous series, as the chain gets longer, the compounds show a _____ change in properties.
e: In a homologous series, as the chain gets longer, the compounds show a gradual change in properties.

q: The general formula is used to represent the _____ of organic compounds.
e: The general formula is used to represent the families of organic compounds.

q: A full structural formula is also known as a graphic formula or _____ formula.
e: A full structural formula is also known as a graphic formula or displayed formula.

q: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon double bond.

q: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon triple bond.

q: An alkane is a compound that _____ functional groups.
e: An alkane is a compound that lacks functional groups.

q: The carbon atom is _____ to all organic compounds.
e: The carbon atom is central to all organic compounds.

q: Organic compounds typically contain other elements in addition to carbon and hydrogen, such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the _____.
e: Organic compounds typically contain other elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the halogens.

q: A homologous series is usually listed in order of increasing _____.
e: A homologous series is usually listed in order of increasing size.

q: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the "_____ hydrocarbons".
e: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the "saturated hydrocarbons".

q: Every carbon in an alkane has a _____ environment and is bonded to four other atoms.
e: Every carbon in an alkane has a tetrahedral environment and is bonded to four other atoms.

q: Alkanes form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alkanes form a homologous series with the general formula $C_nH_{2n+2}$.

q: In the IUPAC nomenclature system, the root name for an organic compound indicates the number of carbon atoms in the _____ continuous chain of carbon atoms.
e: The root name indicates the number of carbon atoms in the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms.

q: When naming alkanes, the C atoms in the longest chain are numbered beginning at the end nearest the _____.
e: Number the C atoms in this longest chain beginning at the end nearest the first branching.

q: Alkyl groups are derived from the corresponding alkanes by the removal of a _____ atom.
e: Alkyl groups are derived from the corresponding alkanes by the removal of a hydrogen atom.

q: Alkyl groups are represented generally as _____, where R is $C_nH_{2n+1}$.
e: Alkyl groups are represented generally as R-, where R is $C_nH_{2n+1}$.

q: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called _____.
e: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms are called isomers.

q: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of _____ isomers.
e: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of structural isomers.

q: All of the alkanes containing _____ or more carbon atoms show structural isomerism.
e: All of the alkanes containing four or more carbon atoms show structural isomerism.

q: In the laboratory, alkanes are prepared by heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with _____.
e: In the laboratory, alkanes are prepared by heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with soda lime.

q: Soda lime is a mixture of calcium oxide (lime) and _____.
e: Soda lime is a mixture of calcium oxide (lime) and sodium hydroxide.

q: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of a catalyst like platinum or _____.
e: The reduction of alkyl halides takes place in the presence of a catalyst like platinum or palladium.

q: The normal alkanes from $C_1$ to $C_4$ are colourless _____.
e: The normal alkanes from $C_1$ to $C_4$ are colourless gases.

q: As the alkane chain gets longer, the boiling points rise, viscosity increases and flammability _____.
e: As the chain gets longer, melting and boiling points rise, viscosity increases and flammability decreases.

q: The most important chemical reactions of saturated hydrocarbons are the substitution and _____ reactions.
e: The most important chemical reactions of these saturated hydrocarbons are the substitution and combustion reactions.

q: When methane is mixed with chlorine in diffused sunlight, a _____ reaction occurs where one chlorine atom replaces one hydrogen atom in each step.
e: When methane is mixed with chlorine in diffused sunlight, a substitution reaction occurs.

q: If there is not enough oxygen, alkanes undergo incomplete combustion, giving off poisonous _____ and less heat energy.
e: If there is not enough oxygen, the alkanes undergo incomplete combustion, giving off poisonous carbon monoxide.

q: The IUPAC system is also known as the _____ System.
e: The IUPAC System is also known as the Geneva System.

q: When naming alkanes, prefixes like di, tri, tetra are used to group _____ substituents.
e: Use the appropriate prefix to group like substituents: di, tri, tetra, penta, and so on.

q: When alphabetizing attached groups in IUPAC naming, prefixes like di and tri are _____ considered.
e: Do not consider these prefixes when alphabetising attached groups.

q: In IUPAC naming, hyphens are used to separate _____ and letters.
e: Use hyphens to separate numbers and letters.

q: The reduction of alkenes is also known as _____.
e: The reduction of alkenes is also known as hydrogenation.

q: Higher temperatures are required for the hydrogenation of alkenes when _____ is used as the catalyst.
e: Higher temperatures are required when nickel is used as the hydrogenating catalyst.

q: Haloalkanes such as $CH_2Cl_2$, $CHCl_3$, and $CCl_4$ are important _____.
e: Haloalkanes such as $CH_2Cl_2$, $CHCl_3$, and $CCl_4$ are important solvents.

q: Alkene molecules are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: Alkene molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond.

q: The ethylenic bond is the _____ group of an alkene, and largely dictates their reactions.
e: This ethylenic bond is the functional group of alkene, and largely dictates their reactions.

q: Alkenes form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alkenes form a homologous series, with the general formula $C_nH_{2n}$.

q: The first member of the alkene series is known as _____.
e: The first member of the series is known as ethene.

q: In the IUPAC system for naming alkenes, the chain is numbered starting at the end nearest to the _____.
e: Number the chain, starting at the end nearest to the double bond.

q: In alkenes, isomers that have the same carbon skeleton and the same functional groups but differ in the location of the functional groups are called _____ isomers.
e: Isomers that differ in the location of the functional groups on the carbon chain are positional isomers.

q: Two methods may be used for the dehydration of alcohols, one of which is heating with concentrated sulphuric acid at _____.
e: When ethanol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 160°C, ethene is formed.

q: Ethene can be prepared from ethanol by passing the vapours over heated alumina ($Al_2O_3$) at _____.
e: Ethene can be prepared from ethanol by passing the vapours over heated alumina at 350°C.

q: Dehydrohalogenation is used when a halogen atom and a hydrogen atom on an adjacent carbon are simultaneously removed as _____.
e: Dehydrohalogenation is used when a halogen atom and a hydrogen atom are simultaneously removed as hydrogen halide.

q: At room temperature, alkenes containing two to four carbon atoms are _____.
e: At room temperature, alkenes containing two to four carbon atoms are gases.

q: Alkenes burn in the air with a luminous, _____ flame.
e: They burn in the air with a luminous, smoky flame.

q: The unsaturated nature of alkenes is shown in their _____ reactions.
e: The unsaturated nature of alkenes is shown in the addition reactions of alkenes.

q: The addition of $Br_2$ to alkenes is used as a simple qualitative test for _____.
e: The addition of $Br_2$ to alkenes is used as a simple qualitative test for unsaturation.

q: When an alkene is added to bromine water, the reddish-brown solution becomes _____ as the $Br_2$ reacts.
e: The reddish-brown solution becomes colourless as the $Br_2$ reacts with the alkene.

q: Markownikoff's rule states that when an unsymmetrical addendum adds on to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part of the addendum adds on to the carbon with the _____ number of hydrogen atoms.
e: The negative part of the addendum adds on to the carbon with the least number of hydrogen atoms.

q: The complete process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing it is called _____.
e: The complete process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing it is called ozonolysis.

q: When ethene is passed into cold dilute potassium permanganate solution, _____ glycol is formed.
e: When ethene is passed into cold dilute potassium permanganate solution, ethene glycol is formed.

q: In the hydroxylation of alkenes, the colour of 1% dilute $KMnO_4$ solution is _____.
e: In this process, the colour of 1% dilute $KMnO_4$ solution is discharged.

q: The common name of ethene is _____.
e: The common name of ethene is ethylene.

q: In the IUPAC naming of alkenes, the number of the first carbon of the double bond is placed directly in front of the _____.
e: Number the first carbon of the double bond directly in front of the root name.

q: Isomers that differ in the structures of the C-skeleton in the longer chain are called _____ isomers.
e: Isomers that differ in the structures of the C-skeleton in the longer chain are chain isomers.

q: Dehydration of alcohols results in the loss of _____.
e: The reaction occurs, resulting in the loss of water.

q: In the dehydrohalogenation of ethyl chloride, the reagent used is an alcoholic solution of _____.
e: When ethyl chloride is heated with an alcoholic solution of potassium hydroxide, ethene is formed.

q: Alkenes are all _____ than water.
e: They are all lighter than water in which they are insoluble.

q: Alkenes are _____ in water.
e: They are all lighter than water in which they are insoluble.

q: Alkyne molecules are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: Alkyne molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond.

q: The acetylenic bond is the functional group of an alkyne, and largely dictates the alkyne _____.
e: This acetylenic bond is the functional group of alkyne, and largely dictates the alkyne reactions.

q: Alkynes form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alkynes form a homologous series, with the general formula $C_nH_{2n-2}$.

q: The first member of the alkyne series is commonly called _____.
e: The first member of the series is known as ethyne. It is commonly called acetylene.

q: The chains with _____ or more carbon atoms in alkynes lead to the formation of structural isomers.
e: The chains with four or more carbon atoms lead to the formation of structural isomers.

q: Calcium carbide reacts with water to produce _____.
e: Calcium carbide reacts with water to produce acetylene (ethyne).

q: Calcium carbide is industrially prepared by heating calcium oxide with _____ in an electric furnace.
e: Calcium carbide is industrially prepared by heating calcium oxide with coke in an electric furnace.

q: At room temperature, alkynes containing five to twelve carbon atoms are _____.
e: At room temperature, alkynes containing five to twelve carbon atoms are liquids.

q: All alkynes are odourless and colourless except ethyne, which has a slightly distinctive _____.
e: They are all odourless and colourless except ethyne which has a slightly distinctive odour.

q: The hydrogenation of an alkyne proceeds in _____ distinct stages.
e: The reaction proceeds in two distinct stages.

q: Chlorine or bromine can be added to ethyne in the _____ to form ethyne di- and tetra-halides.
e: Chlorine or bromine can be added to ethyne in the dark to form ethyne di- and tetra-halides.

q: The addition of water to ethyne with dilute $H_2SO_4$ and $Hg^{2+}$ at 60°C produces _____, via an unstable vinyl alcohol intermediate.
e: The addition of water to ethyne produces ethanal (acetaldehyde) via an unstable vinyl alcohol intermediate.

q: The order of readiness with which hydrogen halides add to ethyne is _____.
e: The order of the readiness with which the hydrogen halides add to ethyne is HI > HBr > HCl > HF.

q: When acetylene is passed over heated sodium, one or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced to form mono- and di- _____.
e: One or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced or substituted by sodium to form mono- and di-sodium acetylides.

q: When ethyne is added to an ammoniacal solution of copper(I) chloride, a _____ precipitate of dicopper acetylide is formed.
e: Ethyne added to an ammoniacal solution of copper(I) chloride forms a red precipitate of dicopper acetylide.

q: When ethyne is added to an ammoniacal solution of silver oxide, a _____ precipitate of disilver acetylide is formed.
e: Ethyne added to an ammoniacal solution of silver oxide forms a white precipitate of disilver acetylide.

q: An alkyne like $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$ contains no hydrogen on the triple bonded carbon and will _____ form metallic acetylides.
e: An alkyne containing no hydrogen on the triple bonded carbon will not form metallic acetylides.

q: The suffix -ane of the alkane is replaced by _____ to name alkynes.
e: The suffix -ane of the alkane is replaced by -yne.

q: Reactions of alkynes can be made to add to the carbon-carbon triple bond or to substitute _____ hydrogens.
e: Reactions can be made to add to carbon-carbon triple bond or to substitute acetylenic hydrogens.

q: The addition reaction of vinyl bromide is in accordance with _____ rule.
e: The addition reaction of vinyl bromide is in accordance with Markownikoff's rule.

q: Alcohols may be considered as derivatives of alkanes where one hydrogen atom is replaced by a _____ group.
e: The replacement of one hydrogen atom in an alkane by a hydroxyl (-OH) group gives the corresponding alcohol.

q: Most of the common reactions of all alcohols are due to the functional group, _____.
e: Most of the common reactions of all alcohols are due to the functional group, -OH.

q: Alcohols form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alcohols form a homologous series with the general formula $C_nH_{2n+1}OH$.

q: In the IUPAC system, the chain of an alcohol is numbered from the end nearest the _____ group.
e: The chain is numbered from the end nearest the -OH group.

q: Alcohols containing at least _____ carbon atoms have more than one structure and form isomers.
e: Alcohols containing at least three carbon atoms have more than one structure.

q: Ethene and steam are passed over a _____ catalyst at 570°C and 60-70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol.
e: Ethene and steam are passed over a phosphoric acid catalyst at 570°C and 60-70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol.

q: In the fermentation method, starch is treated with freshly germinated barley called malt, which contains the enzyme _____.
e: Malt contains the enzyme diastase, which breaks down starch into maltose.

q: The enzyme _____ converts maltose into glucose during fermentation.
e: Yeast secretes maltase which converts maltose into glucose.

q: The enzyme _____ converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation.
e: Yeast secretes zymase which converts glucose into ethanol.

q: The fermented product contains about 11% ethanol and is fractionally distilled to yield rectified spirit containing about _____% ethanol.
e: It is fractionally distilled to yield the rectified spirit of commerce which contains about 95% ethanol.

q: Alcohols from methanol to butanol are mobile liquids, while those above $C_{11}OH$ are usually _____.
e: Those from $C_5OH$ to $C_{11}OH$ are oily liquids, above $C_{11}OH$ they are usually solids.

q: The first two members of the alcohol family, methanol and ethanol, are miscible with water in any _____.
e: The first two members; methanol and ethanol are miscible with water in any proportion.

q: The most toxic member of the alcohol family is _____.
e: The most toxic member is methanol.

q: When a piece of sodium is added to ethanol, reaction occurs at room temperature, liberating _____ gas.
e: When a piece of sodium is added to ethanol, reaction occurs at room temperature, liberating hydrogen.

q: When ethanol is heated with an excess of concentrated sulphuric acid at 160°C, _____ is produced.
e: When ethanol is heated with an excess of concentrated sulphuric acid at 160°C, ethene is produced.

q: When ethanol is heated with a smaller proportion of concentrated sulphuric acid at 140°C, _____ is formed.
e: With a smaller proportion of concentrated sulphuric acid, diethyl ether is formed when the reaction temperature is kept at 140°C.

q: The reaction of an alcohol with an acid to produce an ester and water is called _____.
e: Esterification is a reaction of an alcohol with an acid to produce an ester and water.

q: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester that has a pleasant _____ odour.
e: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester. It has a pleasant fruity odour which is a characteristic of most esters.

q: When ethanol vapour is passed over freshly reduced copper heated at 300°C, removal of hydrogen occurs with the formation of _____.
e: Removal of hydrogen occurs with formation of ethanal (also known as acetaldehyde).

q: When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give _____.
e: Oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give ethanoic acid.
